name: Admin `court` command drops onto the WOLVES vs HAWKS fixture court (sandbox, no energy spent)
description: Smoke test for the title-scope `court` debug command. Every check is a hard waitFor assertion (verified failing via zz-negative-control) rather than a passive extract: the command enters the game scene, the matchup is the deterministic WOLVES/HAWKS fixture, sandbox mode is flagged, the in-game console is reachable, and energy is unchanged after a reload.

steps._comment: bob is the admin — DBG chip only renders for admins
FTUE coach overlay eats clicks if present
BASELINE (hard): energy is full at 5/5 before entering the sandbox

steps.expression: (() => { const el = document.querySelector('[data-testid=debug-input]'); el.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key:'Enter', bubbles:true})); return 'enter-sent'; })()

steps._comment: ASSERTION 1: `court` put us on a live court — no draft, no matchmaking, no energy modal
ASSERTION 2: we genuinely left the lobby (not a court rendered behind it)
ASSERTION 3 (the fixture guarantee): deterministic matchup every run, not a random opponent. Team names are never painted on the court, so this data attribute is the only observable source.
ASSERTION 4: sandbox flag set — this is what suppresses game.end / markFtuePlayed / player-progress writes on exit
Informational: expect 0-0 at Q1 on a fresh court
ASSERTION 5: in-game DBG chip present — required for testMoveAway / testSpinDunk calibration
ASSERTION 6: in-game console accepts commands — the whole point of the sandbox
Bail out of the sandbox the cheap way; a real session would have been persisted server-side by now
ASSERTION 7 (the sandbox payoff): still 5/5 after a server round-trip. Entering the debug court spent no energy and opened no game session.
